summaries: Attest approved Experience Git synchronization through the remote coordination target, preserve local history and staged content, and publish its verified postimage so concurrent readers cannot restore older receipts. Both host contracts and the Requirement flow's handoff name the two accepted forms, `merge --no-edit <source>` and `restore --source=<source> --worktree -- workspace/docs/experience-design`, run with Git's absolute path as a call of its own from the checkout root; when another merge or pull is restored, the guard's message names the restore to run. The remote handoff check bounds each `git ls-remote` to 20 seconds and refuses with the reason and those commands when the remote does not answer.

Merging the pull request that carries a release commit now publishes that release without a command: the new Auto release workflow sees the version change on the push to main and dispatches the Release workflow for the merge commit, while every other push starts nothing; `python3 tools/release.py ship` still starts or resumes a release by hand.

Backlog planning offers the owner only a package atomic approval accepts: check --pre-approval runs approval's own checks, and check refuses a review being written whose verdict field is empty under a concluded Verdict section or contradicts its status.

Open backlog revisions against evolved approved inputs and scaffold fresh review rounds while preserving historical approvals and coverage gates. Opening a revision judges criterion coverage against the BA universe of the last committed backlog approval, in which a topic registry created since then holds no ids, while Delivery still refuses an approved backlog that misses a criterion approved after it. An unchanged approved Story keeps a superseded Solution Design or System Architecture note it cited while that note was approved or accepted.

Process switch `calculation_examples` (`off` | `required`), at its default today's behaviour: at `required`, every business rule that derives a number from inputs or configurable parameters carries its formula in its statement or an AC with a worked example (inputs, parameters, expected output and the output after one parameter change), the analysis challenger reports a missing or inconsistent one as a major finding, and a backlog test plan takes its expected value from that formula or example and never invents one, as `requirements-analysis/references/switch-calculation_examples-required.md` defines for every Business Analysis and Backlog Planning task. In one measured project a scoring rule with no computable expected value cost an analysis round trip of about 63 minutes during a backlog revision.

Stable releases are named by the calendar. A release is `YYYY.M.N`: the UTC year and month in which `python3 tools/release.py bump` made its release commit, the month without a leading zero, and its number within that month from 1, so the first release of October 2026 is `v2026.10.1`, the next `v2026.10.2` and the first of November `v2026.11.1`. `bump` sets the marketplace, every plugin and every version surface to that one version; changeset impacts no longer choose it, and the release metadata still records them. The release commit is dated at the instant `bump` named its version and `check-pr` replays it at that date, so a release commit made at the end of a month stays valid when its pull request merges in the next month, and the release keeps that month's name. With no release tag at all, the Release workflow takes the commit `stable` points to as the previous release instead of the first-release path.

Bind local validation receipts to the variables that can change test behaviour, name the changed variables when verify refuses for that reason, and let verify take the worker count of the receipt's check.
Keep a local validation receipt valid when another worktree of the same repository creates, tracks, fetches or deletes branches during the run.

CI runs each test shard in three worker processes, each with its own temporary directory and host tripwires, and balances the tests over every process by their measured durations. The Windows minimum-version lane installs its pinned python.org NuGet build of Python instead of running the setup-python installer, and Windows tests keep their scratch files on the runner's work disk.

CI splits the full Linux test runs into more shards and runs only the platform group on the current macOS lane, whose full suite every contributor already runs in the local gate, so a pull request checks in about half the time.
Fetch complete Git history in generated vault and verification CI jobs so earlier approved evidence remains readable.

On Codex the `-mechanical` writer variants keep running on the `low` tier, `gpt-6.1-sol` at effort `xhigh`, until the variants' frozen-task A/B sets a lower effort. Under process switch `mechanical_pass_tier` at `mechanical`, the Codex host contract starts the variant for every `apply_findings` pass and never resumes the base writer for one, and the mechanical pass record names whether the variant or the resumed writer ran, with its model and effort, so the A/B and later passes show the tier that really ran. At every switch default no role changes. In one measured project a Codex fix pass that rewrote a single numeric test ran about 16 minutes at the writers' effort.

New read-only `experience_compile.py source-impact --root <experience-design> --source-ref business-analysis/<space>/space` lists every approved Experience package that binds the source's receipt, the source rows and documents that changed since that receipt, the package notes that cite them, and per package whether it is a `mechanical` rebind, when no note cites a change, or a `semantic` one, and whether its open revision changed anything besides the source receipts. Process switch `dependent_rebind_gate` (`separate` | `with_source`), at its default today's behaviour: at `with_source`, the gate that approves a business-analysis change opens with one plain sentence of the whole action and also approves the mechanical Experience rebinds it makes necessary, which then run without a second scope gate while `source-impact` still reports a receipt-only change, as `business-analysis/references/switch-dependent_rebind_gate-with_source.md` defines; a semantic dependent keeps its own gate. In one measured project such a second gate asked nothing new and stayed open 4 h 19 min.

Process switch `epic_review_cadence` (`wait_per_panel` | `overlap_calibration`), off by default, so every default output and every bound instruction is unchanged. At `overlap_calibration`, when backlog epic reviews queue behind the host's agent limit, the next epic review starts as soon as the previous review's last reader returns; at `review_loop` `blocking_delta` a calibration reader starts for each reader's critical and major claims as soon as that reader returns, and each claim is still ruled once by a fresh reader on the claiming reviewer's role and tier; the coordinator writes only a fixed JSON claim record at a review boundary; and no writer action starts until every epic review and every calibration has returned. In one measured project, four panel transitions of one backlog revision lost 32.7 min to the severity check and the coordinator's record keeping, and the one transition that overlapped the check took 1.6 min.

The local pre-push gate runs only the change's own tests within a budget of about three minutes, with four workers that call Git directly on macOS, names failing tests last and keeps their logs; pull request CI runs every test on Linux and macOS.

A Delivery role that waits on the Item no longer sleeps past the host's prompt cache. Nothing told a role how to wait for a verification command, so readers improvised loops of up to ten minutes, the longest foreground timeout Claude Code allows, while the prompt cache lives five minutes: each wake-up wrote the reader's whole context into the cache again, and in one measured project those rewrites were about 47% of the list price of a Delivery's six readers. `delivery_verification.py` gains `wait`: `wait --role code_reviewer|qa_engineer` returns once that reader's own verification command has exited, `wait` alone once no command holds the Item's environment or verification command lock, each call as soon as that happens and at the latest after the verification policy's new `wait_bound_seconds`, 240 seconds, with the holder it still waits for. The Delivery flow and both host contracts make `wait`, called again as its own tool call, the only way a role waits, and long commands start in the background; the refusals that leave a role waiting name `wait`, the reader barrier lets `wait` through, and `tools/validate.py` keeps the bound between 60 and 270 seconds. The code reviewer, which runs no command, registers its finished result at once and returns, and a reader whose result waits for another role's step, such as a calibration, returns it unregistered for the coordinator. What a registration waits for is unchanged.

The local pre-push gate selects the changed test methods and the tests that name a changed input or function, runs static checks beside the test workers and keeps the change's own tests within about 40 seconds.
CI balances its shards on the durations a full run measured on each system.
The macOS CI lane runs the tests that prove macOS behavior again, as one shard; running every test there took pull request CI from 2 min 32 s to 6 to 7.5 minutes.

Backlog commands read each Git commit once per process. `backlog_compile.py` read the same committed backlog tree, BA registry listing and blob again for every approval and history check; these reads are now kept for the process by resolved repository path, object id and arguments. HEAD is still resolved on every call, every read keeps `--no-replace-objects`, a failed read is not kept and each caller gets its own copy, so results are unchanged. In one measured run a single `stub-backlog-review` started 12 instead of 26 Git processes, and the backlog pre-approval test module 340 instead of 812.
At own_target_reuse spot_run, QA's final test run without a spot-run file says why it reuses no own target even when it reuses nothing else or no pre-handoff run exists.
Open fresh policy-aware root and epic review rounds and approve only current completed reviews, preserving unapproved history, approved evidence and source bytes.
Every pull request and merge queue group runs the full test suite in CI; main reuses that proof for the identical tree.

The plugin supports Python 3.14 only. Every hook now runs through a small launcher that checks the Python version before anything else: below 3.14 the plugin stops only its own work, with one message that names the Python it found, the fix (macOS: `brew install python3`) and a session restart, and it never blocks the host session, other prompts or any tool call that is not the plugin's own work. CI tests one Python per operating system.

Two process switches shorten a Delivery's QA gate, both off by default, so every default output and every bound instruction is unchanged. Process switch `own_target_reuse` (`off` | `spot_run`): at `spot_run`, where `pre_handoff_regression` at `touched_suites` gave the freeze an accepted pre-handoff run, QA's final `delivery_verification.py run --kind test --spot-run-file <file>` also takes the Item's own Test Plan targets from that run, under the bindings the earlier stories' targets already need (frozen tree, derived selection and approved command, QA's declared environment, final-evidence age), but for the own targets QA names in the spot-run selection and every own target that is, prefixes or lies under one of them, or under such a target in turn, which the approved test command runs. The runner refuses a spot-run file outside the verification scratch, one that binds another candidate or names a target outside the Item's own Test Plan, and the option with `--fresh`, with any kind but `test` and at `off`; the run's identity records the reused own targets and the spot-run targets under `reused_pre_handoff.own_targets`, evidence approval checks them as recorded, and `approve-item-evidence` adds them to the Item's verification record. Its switch reference asks QA to audit the reused targets with the accepted run's JUnit and output. In one measured project, the story's own cases took 163 of the 227 minutes of QA's final test run, and about 94% of that run repeated tests already run on the identical tree before the handoff. Process switch `qa_gate_order` (`plan_first` | `gate_first`): at `gate_first`, QA starts its first test command of a round in the background, plans, maps and drafts its result while the command works, reads the output only once its plan and coverage matrix are written and waits for the command only through `wait --role qa_engineer`; in one measured project QA spent 12 to 18 minutes per round writing after a gate of several hours. The `touched_suites` reference now states that the pre-handoff run, like QA's first gate, reports every failing group and counts a group that fails to collect as a failed one.

Process switch `reader_waves` (`as_slots_free` | `all_at_once`), at its default today's behaviour: at `all_at_once`, a review or recheck wave of Backlog Planning, Business Analysis, Design System, Execution Planning, Operation or Solution Design starts every reader before waiting on any, as the new switch reference `challenge-review/references/switch-reader_waves-all_at_once.md` defines for every task of those flows. On Codex the coordinator first closes every finished agent thread, a writer between its passes included, because every open spawned thread counts against the session's thread cap; when threads are short it starts the largest inputs first, and every wave's progress message names its size and readers running at once. In one measured project a 12-reader recheck wave ran in batches of at most three for 51 min against a slowest reader of 20.7 min.

Process switch `rebind_review_scope` (`full` | `source_delta`), at its default today's behaviour: at `source_delta`, when `experience_compile.py source-impact` reports that an Experience revision only moved its source receipts (`source_rebind_only`) and no package note cites a changed source row or document, the fresh `experience-reviewer` reads the source diff, the package notes and the attested hashes instead of the prototype tree, reports any claim that depends on the changed source, which starts the full review, and writes the same schema-v4 attestation, as `experience-modeling/references/switch-rebind_review_scope-source_delta.md` defines. In one measured project the full review of such a rebind took about 28 minutes and 70.3 M input tokens to confirm the zero changed bytes the compiler had proved in 2 minutes.

As released, the local pre-push gate runs a change's own tests in about 40 seconds and pull request CI runs every test on Linux, with the tests that prove macOS and Windows behavior on those systems; the Windows minimum-version lane and its NuGet Python left with the move to Python 3.14.

Process switch `remediation_bookkeeping` (`writer` | `compiler`), off by default, so every default output and every bound instruction is unchanged. At `compiler`, a backlog remediation writer does content fixes only and runs `backlog_compile.py record-rechecks --closures <file> --candidate <reviewed commit> --report <file>` once: from the recheck readers' closure tables, copied verbatim into one JSON file, it writes each current review note's `Recheck Closures` table (finding, reader, closed or open, the manifest hash the reader read, cited evidence), derives the expected review manifest hash of every touched epic and the root, and writes a preservation report of every backlog file changed, added, removed or kept byte for byte since the candidate, failing on an approved review the candidate holds. It refuses an approved note and a row whose finding `Returned Findings` does not list, is idempotent, and `--verify` writes nothing and fails on a hand-edited table or a stale report; `backlog_compile.py check` validates the rows of a draft review note at this value only. In one measured project, this bookkeeping took about 26 and 18 min of two writer passes of one backlog revision on the highest tier.

Process switch `remediation_writers` (`single_writer` | `per_epic`), off by default, so every default manifest, task and bound instruction is unchanged. At `per_epic`, after every epic review returns, each epic with accepted findings gets its own Product Owner writer, in parallel within the host's agent limit: its `task_inputs.py --epic` task reads that epic's review scope at the `review_manifest_scope` value in force, so at `bounded` the epic reader's read set, names `remediation_writers: per_epic` and writes only that epic's notes. Findings that name notes of several epics, the backlog root or the backlog as a whole go afterwards to one cross-epic writer, derived without `--epic` but with `--findings`, whose write scope is exactly the notes it is given with `--input`. A writer that only applies named fixes may run as the Product Owner's mechanical variant under `mechanical_pass_tier`. In one measured project, the single writer was bound to 1,063 inputs and 21.5 MB of sources, read for about 88 min, compacted its context 7 times and had changed no canonical file after 96 min.

Remove the vault hook's trust path for Apple's /usr/bin/python3 launcher: the hooks require Python 3.14 and the Apple system launcher can no longer run them, so it is refused like any other foreign interpreter.

Process switch `review_scope_record` (`off` | `both_scopes`), off by default, so every default manifest and every bound instruction is unchanged. At `both_scopes`, `backlog_review_inputs.py --epic` also derives the epic's manifest under the other `review_manifest_scope` value and adds `scope_sizes` to the reader's manifest: files, source bytes and manifest bytes of both read sets, and, when the owner sets the switch's `transitive_source_bytes` parameter, whether the transitive read set exceeds it, which the flow shows before any reader starts and answers with a choice gate offering `bounded`. `--scope-findings` lists the review's blocking findings, after calibration, with the notes each cites and those outside the bounded read set, read from the review note's Returned Findings or a `--findings` claim record, and `--record` appends either measurement as a JSON line to the tracked record `<workspace>/measurements/review-scope.jsonl`, beside the docs vault; another file must lie in the workspace outside the vault, and a file Git ignores is refused. In one measured project, a 23-story epic's transitive read set handed each reader 1,002 files and 21.6 MB of sources against 8.9 MB bounded, and the discarded first panel cost 64 min.

Process switch `root_review_scope` (`full` | `revision_delta`), off by default, so every default manifest, task and bound instruction is unchanged. At `revision_delta`, with the owner's `max_delta_share_percent` parameter, `backlog_review_inputs.py --root` derives a revision's delta from the approval stamps: every story whose story or test plan is new or no longer carries the stamp of its bytes, and every story one dependency edge away from one. The root reader's manifest then names in full only those stories and test plans with the sources they link to, the backlog root, every epic, each epic's current review and the root review notes, and its `check` carries the root review's compiler facts and `backlog_graph`: every story with its epic, title, criteria, scenario count, dependencies and the hashes of its story and test plan, and every dependency edge. The manifest's hash still binds every backlog byte. A first backlog, a delta over the owner's share and a reader's request, passed as `--full-root-reason` to `backlog_review_inputs.py --root` or a `task_inputs.py --epic` root task, read the whole package with the reason recorded in `revision_delta`. In one measured project, a revision that added four stories to 110 ran a root panel of 98.4 min and about 760 M input tokens that found three minor record fixes.

Process switch `source_decision_gate` (`two_gates` | `one_gate_when_drafted`), at its default today's behaviour: at `one_gate_when_drafted`, a decision that changes approved analysis documents and whose recommended option needs no owner input is drafted and independently reviewed before the owner is asked, and one gate shows the options with the reviewed diff and content hash of the recommended one as "approve this exact change"; any other answer falls back to two gates, as `business-analysis/references/switch-source_decision_gate-one_gate_when_drafted.md` defines. New `ba_compile.py content-hash --space <space>` hashes a space's authored content without lifecycle stamps, status tags, generated relations or generated views, so a reviewed draft and the package approved from it share it, and `approve-package --expected-content-hash <hash>` refuses, without writing, content that differs from what the gate showed. In one measured project one source decision took a 19 min direction gate and a 2 h 10 min exact-change gate for a change that was ready with zero findings.

Process switch `test_cost_budget` (`off` | `flag_serial_rows`), off by default, so every default output and every bound instruction is unchanged. A Test Plan scenario may state `rows`, the table rows its automation target runs, and `row_split`, `serial`, `sharded` or `grouped`; `backlog_compile.py check` refuses a `rows` value that is no positive integer and any other split whenever a scenario states them, at every value. At `flag_serial_rows`, with the owner's `serial_rows` limit set through `/configure process` (the package recommends none), `backlog_compile.py check --json`, the epic and root review manifests and `delivery_compile.py init` list under `test_cost` each automation-required scenario whose rows exceed the limit while its split is `serial` or absent, with its story and automation target. The flag is advisory and never fails a check. Its switch reference, bound for every Backlog Planning and Delivery Planning task at that value only, has QA propose a sharded or grouped split before the epic review, or the owner keep the scenario serial with a reason recorded in the review note. In one measured project, one test ran 260 rows serially for 58 minutes, 25% of QA's final gate.

Process switch `test_engines` (`single` | `partitioned`), single by default, so every default output and every bound instruction is unchanged. A Verification Contract may declare `test_partition_command`, `test_engines` and a `Test Partitions` table (partition, groups, profile), all or none, with optional `shared_profiles`; `operation_compile.py check` refuses a partial declaration, a group of `test_groups` in no partition or in two, an undeclared group and a shared profile the table does not use, and an Environment Contract may declare the same `test_engines`. At `partitioned`, with the partition command declared and every engine provisioned by the Environment Contract, `delivery_verification.py run --kind test` runs each partition in its own private clone with `AGENTROF_TEST_PARTITION`, a JSON file holding the candidate hash, the partition, its groups, its engine and the reused test ids, `AGENTROF_TEST_ENGINE` and its own scratch directory, longest first by its last recorded duration, never two partitions of an exclusive profile on one engine at once and never more partitions than engines, under the Item's environment lock until the last one ends. A failing partition, or one that cannot start, never stops another; one record lists every partition's engine, exit code, intactness, duration and output, its exit code is 0 only when every partition passed intact, and its identity binds the plan, the partition command and the declared environment, not the schedule. Evidence approval refuses a record that lacks a partition, holds one twice, holds a failed or not intact one or ran another command. No other command receives the two partition variables, an inherited one included. `regression-run` and diagnostic runs stay one command. In one measured project, QA's final gate ran 227 minutes for 166 cases on one engine, which was busy for at least 64% of the Delivery's wall clock.

Process switch `test_group_report` (`off` | `refuse_missing_groups`), off by default, so every default output and every bound instruction is unchanged. A Verification Contract may declare `test_groups`, the group ids its test command runs, and `test_group_report`, the file the command writes under `AGENTROF_VERIFICATION_SCRATCH` with each group's status (`passed`, `failed` or `not_collected`) and case counts; `operation_compile.py check` takes both or neither, the groups as unique literal ids and the report as a normalized relative path. At `refuse_missing_groups`, with both declared, `delivery_verification.py run --kind test`, `run --kind diagnostic_test` and `regression-run` remove any earlier report before the command, then record each declared group's status in the run record, which the run result and `status` print, record a run whose report lacks a declared group not intact and name it, and bind the declaration in the run's identity; `freeze` names the groups a refused pre-handoff run's report lacked, and evidence approval refuses a final test run with a group that is missing, not collected or failed. In one measured project, QA's first gate ran 58 of the suite's 166 cases because the command stopped at its first failure and two groups never collected, and five of the seven blockers of the next repair sat in tests that round never ran.

The test suite runs faster with the same product guards. CI runs every test on Linux and, on macOS and Windows, only the tests that prove behavior of that system. Validator mutation tests run the one check they target; setup, project vault, Delivery PR-intent, Experience record revision and CI plan tests copy a prepared fixture instead of rebuilding it; the coordinator's verb help renders in process. Stale and redundant tests are gone, the process switches' sentence-copying tests become one registry-driven check plus the safety rules each switch value keeps, and model tests read model IDs from the shipped catalogs.

The concurrent setup test no longer fails on a loaded machine. It required two setup applies started together to both succeed, which held only while the first finished within setup's 3-second guard wait. The test now holds the guard until both applies wait for it, so they always contend, and gives each a wait as long as its process timeout; a new test keeps setup's own 3-second bound and its maintenance_busy refusal.

Add a compact `delivery_verification.py status --summary` and `status --run <kind>` that print the session identity, reader states and run outcomes with their report paths, and point the reader instructions at them instead of the whole session.
